A1.justification: Both complete 15-page PDFs describe the same WLKS research. Their text, equations, Tables 1–5, Figures 1–5, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original WLKS classification, runtime, ablation, and sensitivity results in Sections 5–6, plus a structural-encoding experiment in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains original WLKS classification, runtime, ablation, and sensitivity results, including the structural-encoding experiment in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The WLS/WLKS algorithms, kernel combinations, hop selection, continuous-feature integration, and Appendix D structural-encoding approach are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight datasets: PPI-BP, HPO-Neuro, HPO-Metab, EM-User, Density, Cut-Ratio, Coreness, and Component. No task, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains SubGNN, GLASS, VSubGAE, SSNP-NN, and the GCNII-based S2N+0 and S2N+A comparators. Table 3 also retains the same runtime comparators and participation.

E3.justification: Table 1 preserves the dataset sizes and splits: 80/10/10 except EM-User at 70/15/15. The micro-F1 metric, hyperparameter searches, model configurations, and runtime-measurement procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 4–5 retain the hop-set and feature-integration analyses; Figures 3–4 retain iteration and mixing-coefficient sensitivity analyses. Appendix D's random-walk structural-encoding experiment is already present in v1.

E5.justification: Both versions report means over 10 runs and standard deviations in Tables 2 and 5. Table 4 omits standard deviations because all are zero. No run-count or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains WLKS micro-F1 scores of 64.8 on PPI-BP and 91.8 on EM-User; Appendix D retains the same Cut-Ratio improvement from 60.0 to 96.0 with structural encoding.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Propositions 3.1–3.2 and their proofs, kernel-combination equations, and computational-complexity analysis are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about novelty, expressiveness, classification performance, and computational efficiency. The publication-status update introduces no scientific claim.

C2.justification: Section 6 and Appendices A–D preserve the same interpretations and qualifications concerning structural expressiveness, feature-versus-structure tradeoffs, hop selection, and the limited cross-dataset benefits of structural encoding.

D1.justification: The code-access footnote, software frameworks, SVM implementation, hardware, hyperparameter ranges, and Appendix D walk-length details are unchanged. The new funding acknowledgment adds no implementation or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning in Section 2 and the appendices are unchanged. References moving between pages 10–12 are retained entries, not additions or removals.

P1.justification: v2 replaces the running 'Preprint' header with 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025,' updates the arXiv version/date stamp, and adds a funding acknowledgment after the conclusion. Scientific prose and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgment causes minor spacing adjustments on page 10 and bibliography reflow across pages 10–12. All five figures and five tables retain their content and structure; Figure 4 shifts slightly vertically.

improvement.justification: v2 adds funding attribution and updates publication metadata, with minor layout adjustments. The scientific content, supporting evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, so these administrative edits do not materially alter overall paper quality.
